subject: How to avoid endless loop in shiny

messages.author: 91f026bb2871a7ee
messages.subject: How to avoid endless loop in shiny
parts:
Hi, 

I added two sliderInput into the app with package "shiny": sliderA and sliderB. The values in the two sliders are correlated. If I change sliderA, I used updateSliderInput to update the value in sliderB. And also If I change sliderB, I used  updateSliderInput to update the value in slideA. 

The problem is it is an endless loop. How can I use updateSliderInput without sending message to update the other slider.

messages.author: 91f026bb2871a7ee
messages.subject: Re: How to avoid endless loop in shiny
parts:
I just found out the reason. 

After I change sliderA, sliderB will be updated with updateSliderInput. Then sliderB will send a message to update sliderA again. If sliderA is asked to update to the same value, the will be nor further messages. But I set sliderA to update to another value. Endless loop.

messages.subject: Re: How to avoid endless loop in shiny
parts:
There is still a problem.

For the following code:

server <- function(input, output, clientData, session) {
  observeEvent(input$sliderA,{
    
    st <- max(1, as.integer((input$sliderB[1]+input$sliderB[2] - input$sliderA)/2))
    ed <- min(1500, st + input$sliderA - 1)
    if(ed == 1500){
      st = ed - input$sliderA + 1
    }
    updateSliderInput(session, "sliderB", value = c(st,ed))
  })
  
  
  observeEvent(input$sliderB,{
    updateSliderInput(session, "sliderA", value = input$sliderB[2] - input$sliderB[1] + 1)
  })
}


sliderB may update more than one time since siderA may give different value for sliderB to update. How can I suspend sending message when using updateSliderInput?

messages.subject: Re: How to avoid endless loop in shiny
parts:
Oh, that helps. Maybe something like this (note, this is one of the only times I've ever suggested modifying a session-level non-reactive variable [ignoreNext]):

ignoreNext <- ""

observeEvent(input$sliderA, {
  if (ignoreNext == "A") {
    ignoreNext <<- ""
  }

  valB <- ...

  if (valB != input$sliderB) {
    ignoreNext <<- "B"
    updateSliderInput(session, "sliderB", value = valB)
  }
})

observeEvent(input$sliderB, {
  if (ignoreNext == "B") {
    ignoreNext <<- ""
  }

  valA <- ...

  if (valA != input$sliderA) {
    ignoreNext <<- "A"
    updateSliderInput(session, "sliderA", value = valA)
  }
})

You might also consider something like plotly, rbokeh, or dygraphs, which all have built-in zooming, or something like this for ggplot2 (see the "Interactive Plots" section of the articles page).
